transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-08 15:00 UTC / Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Riley Brooks (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (ZephyrSearch - Head of Search), Marc Diaz (Eng Manager), Sonia Patel (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, and with me is Riley, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Olivia: Doing well thanks, excited to see the embeddings and rerank flow. We chatted a bit with sales earlier but wanted a deeper look at relevance.
[00:15] Riley: Great, we'll walk through the hosted embeddings API, then the rerank endpoint, and show a simple integration pattern with Elastic or your current search stack. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Marc: Quick FYI — our current traffic is bursty, avg 40 qps but peaks to 120 qps, and 95th pct latency needs to be under ~200ms for user search.
[00:40] Sonia: And we store all logs on-prem, we prefer hosted but need SOC2 + KMS for keys, and want to understand data retention policies.

Auto-summary / goals section (auto-generated):
- Demo embeddings generation and rerank scoring flow.
- Show typical latency numbers and batching behavior.
- Discuss security concerns: SOC2, KMS, VPC options.
- Agree pilot next steps and benchmark plan.

[03:02] Riley: Ok jumping in — on the embeddings side we have a hosted API that returns vector embeddings, supports batch upsert, and has semantic similarity helpers. Example SDK call is two lines, or curl. For rerank, we provide a dedicated endpoint that takes your query + candidate doc texts and returns relevance scores — useful to do a lightweight re-ranking stage after Elastic search results.
[03:35] Olivia: So we would still keep Elastic as the initial retrieval layer, then call Redwood rerank for top-k?
[03:42] Avery: Exactly — typical pattern is recall with Elastic, then rerank top 50 with embeddings or a rerank model. You only pay for the rerank calls which are smaller than full indexing.
[04:10] Marc: What about latency for that two-step approach — if we recall then rerank 50, what's the end-to-end impact?
[04:18] Riley: Good Q. For hosted we see median rerank latency in the 30-80ms range for small payloads, depends on model size and sequence length. With continuous batching it can be even better during high throughput, but tail can go up if many large documents. Our 95th pct SLA for dedicated customers is tighter; hosted has documented profiles.
[04:46] Sonia: Are model sizes fixed? We want better quality but worried about cost.
[04:52] Avery: We recommend using a medium-sized embedding model for most semantic rerank use cases — you get good quality/cost balance. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching to reduce cost.

[07:15] Riley: Demo time — I'm pasting a quick sample: we send the query, the top-k docs, the rerank endpoint returns a score list. (screen share) — note here the API supports streaming token outputs for text generation, but for rerank it's a synchronous score response.
[07:40] (small pause, typing)
[08:00] Olivia: I'm seeing the payload size — can we send metadata IDs only and let Redwood fetch doc text from an S3 link?
[08:08] Riley: We don't fetch arbitrarily from S3 for hosted calls for security reasons; typically you'd send the snippet or call with pre-fetched text. For private deployments we can add connectors. You can also store doc vectors in our vector store or bring your own.

[10:12] Marc: On throughput — if we do 120 qps peak and do rerank top 50 for 20% of queries, that's ~12 rerank calls per sec. Any rate limiting concerns?
[10:22] Avery: Hosted handles that but you should expect some throttling at very high sustained peaks. For production scale with predictable throughput, Dedicated is recommended — reserved GPU pools give predictable latency and throughput and you can set autoscaling/burst policies.

[12:00] Sonia: About embeddings consistency — if we re-generate embeddings over time and we have re-index jobs, will we see drift? How do you handle versioning?
[12:10] Riley: We support model version pinning and rollouts; you can pin to a version and run A/B reindexing. Redwood Optimize can recommend which quantization to use and flag quality regressions against your eval sets.

[14:30] (Riley walks through SDK example and console screenshot)
[14:46] Riley: In the Console you can see per-route latency, cost-per-token, and token-level breakdowns. For rerank we show per-request vector compute time.
[15:05] Olivia: Can we get per-customer or per-team RBAC in the Console? We want separate teams to have restricted access.
[15:12] Avery: Yes, RBAC with SSO/SAML and audit logs is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has team-level controls and admin roles.

[18:00] Marc: Security — we need SOC2 and ISO docs, and we use AWS KMS for keys. How does Redwood integrate?
[18:08] Riley: We are SOC2 certified; for hosted we manage keys, but we also support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM for Private deployments. We'll share the security pack after this call.

[20:20] Olivia: Data residency — some queries must remain in EU region. Do you support region pinning?
[20:28] Avery: Yes, hosted supports region-specific endpoints; Dedicated and Private give you full region control.

[22:00] (Demo continues — rerank ranking differences shown)
[23:30] Sonia: The rerank scores look good, can you show thresholding or confidence outputs?
[23:38] Riley: We return a normalized score; you can apply thresholds client-side. For more advanced flows we have function outputs and structured responses to help with downstream decisions.

[26:15] Marc: For the pilot, we'd like to run against anonymized recent query logs to compare relevancy lift vs current Elastic ranking. Can Redwood run that benchmark or do we run scripts?
[26:25] Avery: We can help run an initial benchmark as part of a short POC — Riley will prepare scripts and a test plan. We'll need a sample of anonymized queries and candidate doc sets.

[29:00] (Short side conversation about cost)
[29:15] Olivia: Cost is important — hosted per-call can add up, how do we estimate TCO?
[29:22] Avery: We'll send a TCO spreadsheet comparing hosted vs Dedicated for your projected qps and rerank rate. Optimize can find batching/quantization to save 30-60% depending on patterns.

[31:40] Riley: Quick note on caching — prefix/KV caching can help for repeated queries, and our smart routing can fallback to cheaper model variants during congestion to keep availability. That helps keep the experience smooth during spikes.

[34:10] Sonia: Any pitfalls or common integration gotchas?
[34:18] Riley: Two common ones — sending unnecessarily large doc snippets (trim to relevant fields) and not batching candidate docs. Also watch sequence length; long contexts increase latency. We often recommend a short snippet + metadata for rerank.

[36:50] (Avery shares sample contract terms and pilot pricing)
[37:10] Olivia: Timeline — we hope to decide within 3 weeks. Pilot would need to start asap to get results before next planning cycle.
[37:20] Avery: Sounds good, we'll aim to have pricing and security docs by tomorrow, and Riley will get the benchmark plan by next week.

[40:00] (Customer asks about observability hooks)
[40:08] Riley: Console exposes per-route dashboards, traces, and token-level cost. You can also export traces to your telemetry stack.

[42:30] Marc: One last technical thing — do you support on-prem connectors or private deployment to our VPC?
[42:38] Avery: Yes, Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem, and Dedicated can be run in partner regions with customer networking. We'll include deployment options in the security pack.

[45:00] (Wrap-up demo, brief Q&A)
[46:15] Olivia: Okay, recap — send TCO and pricing, security docs, trial API key, and we will share anonymized query logs. Schedule the SE benchmark session next Tue.
[46:30] Avery: Correct. Action items: Avery sends pricing/TCO & security docs, Riley prepares scripts and plan, Olivia shares logs.

[48:00] (audio glitch, minor overlap)
[49:12] Sonia: Quick thought — we might want to try rerank only on web search first and then expand to recommendations.
[49:20] Avery: That's a common phased approach and reduces risk and cost.

[51:00] Marc: Thanks everyone, this was useful.
[51:06] Olivia: Thanks, talk soon.
[51:10] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and kickoff docs.

End of transcript.
